title: Restriction along a coefficient isomorphism preserves K-flatness
statement: Let $T$ be a scheme and let $R,S$ be sheaves of commutative rings on its pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site, def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Let $e:R\simeq S$ be a ring-sheaf isomorphism. For every K-flat cochain complex $P$ of $S$-module sheaves [def-pc-kflat-complex], termwise restriction of scalars along $e$ [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars] is a K-flat cochain complex of $R$-modules. There is no boundedness or termwise-flatness hypothesis.

source.place: Tag 06YN, definition-K-flat; Tag 0G7E, scalar-extension preservation; recorded step 7 of lem-trf-point-quotient-tower-homotopy, coefficient transport along the completed ring isomorphism

proof.text: Apply K-flat preservation for ordinary scalar extension to the inverse ring-sheaf isomorphism e.inv, using the published reductionChange object and morphism identifications. This gives a K-flat complex over R.

The sectionwise restriction compositors and identity restriction isomorphism make restriction along e.hom and e.inv inverse equivalences. In particular restriction along e.hom is left adjoint to restriction along e.inv. Ordinary extension along e.inv has this same right adjoint, so uniqueness of left adjoints gives a natural isomorphism between it and restriction along e.hom. Map this to cochain complexes and tensor with every acyclic test complex; the resulting isomorphism transports acyclicity. This includes the identity isomorphism and zero complex.
